column1: # Rise of Empires 1444: war fleets of the mid-15th century. All counts are rounded
# estimates of oared war galleys (and for the Atlantic powers armed round ships and caravels) that
# a state kept or could readily arm; they all become galleys (1 unit = 10 ships) in the game.

column15: note
Arsenal war galleys (Gulf guard; Romania and Candia squadrons) plus armed merchant galleys; the Arsenal could arm about 100; moderate confidence
Communal and Maona of Chios galleys; Genoese fleets were largely privately armed; low confidence
Gallipoli fleet of galleys and fustae after the 1444 Dardanelles crossing; 1453 accounts give 100+ vessels including transports; low confidence
Catalan and Sicilian galleys of Alfonso V; low confidence
Neapolitan royal galleys; low confidence
Biscayan naos and Seville galleys; low confidence
Royal galleys plus armed caravels; low confidence
Royal galleys at Rouen-Harfleur and Marseille-Aigues-Mortes; speculative
The royal fleet had been sold off after 1422; impressed armed merchantmen; speculative
Philip the Good's crusading galleys (several sent to the Black Sea in 1444-45); low confidence
Danish royal and levy ships; speculative
Galleys used against Rhodes (1440-44); low confidence
Hospitaller galleys at Rhodes; moderate confidence
A handful of imperial galleys; moderate confidence
Coastal guard war junks after the end of the treasure voyages (the full establishment was far larger); low confidence
Joseon naval garrisons (Sejong-era registers list several hundred mostly small vessels); low confidence
Lê river and coastal war boats; speculative
Malaccan war prahus; speculative
Javanese jong and war prahus; speculative
Gujarati war vessels at Diu and Cambay; speculative
Zamorin's paros (light war boats); speculative
Hormuzi war boats; speculative
